documents.name: Russian biometric international passport (zagranpasport)
documents.description: Original Russian foreign-travel passport valid at least 3 months beyond the intended stay (many consulates require 6+ months) with at least two blank pages. Applications from Russian citizens are accepted only for the passport holder in person at the Moscow centre or at a Portuguese consulate where the applicant holds legal residence.

documents.name: Completed Portuguese national (type D) visa application form
documents.description: Official national visa form, signed by the applicant; downloadable in Portuguese or Russian from the Embassy of Portugal in Moscow. Note: the remote-work/digital-nomad category is commonly called D8, but the Moscow BLS checklist lists remote-work 'digital nomads' under a separate code — confirm the exact category label when booking.

documents.name: Two biometric passport photos (35x45 mm)
documents.description: Two recent identical colour photographs meeting Portuguese consular photo specifications; submitted with the paper file in addition to the fingerprints and digital photo captured at the visa centre.

documents.name: Photocopies of every passport page and of each supporting document
documents.description: The Moscow visa centre requires a separate photocopy of every page of the passport and of each document in the file, submitted alongside the originals. This is distinct from the biometric photos above.

documents.name: Russian criminal record certificate with apostille and sworn Portuguese translation
documents.description: Certificate of absence of criminal record issued by the Russian Ministry of Internal Affairs (ГИАЦ МВД), issued within the last 3 months, legalised with a Hague apostille and translated into Portuguese by a certified/sworn translator. Allow several weeks; translation requirements can vary by consular post — verify with the Embassy in Moscow.
documents.source: Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation (ГИАЦ МВД) / Embassy of Portugal in Moscow

documents.name: Signed authorisation for AIMA to consult the Portuguese criminal record
documents.description: Standard consent form permitting the Portuguese immigration authority to check the applicant's criminal record in Portugal; submitted with the visa file.

documents.name: Proof of remote professional activity for a non-Portuguese employer or clients
documents.description: Employment contract, secondment/remote-work declaration from the employer, or freelance/service contracts and invoices with clients established outside Portugal, showing the work is performed remotely. Documents in Russian require translation (Portuguese, or English where accepted).

documents.name: Proof of monthly income at four times the Portuguese minimum wage
documents.description: Payslips, invoices or bank credit records for the last 3 consecutive months evidencing average monthly income of at least four times the Portuguese minimum wage (threshold is indexed and rises annually; higher amounts apply if dependants are included) — confirm the current figure with the consulate before submission.

documents.name: Bank statements showing accumulated savings
documents.description: Statements for the last 3–6 months, stamped/certified by the bank, showing a savings balance equal to roughly twelve months of the Portuguese minimum wage. Russian-bank statements are accepted as proof of means, but sanctions may restrict later transfers to Portugal — consider holding funds in an account outside Russia and verify acceptance with the consular post.

documents.name: Russian tax residence / tax return evidence
documents.description: Tax residence certificate or filed personal income tax return (e.g. 3-NDFL or self-employed/IP tax statement) confirming that the declared income is taxed outside Portugal. Some consulates ask for 12 months of tax residence proof; verify with the official source as practice varies.

documents.name: Proof of accommodation in Portugal
documents.description: Signed Portuguese lease agreement (12 months is the safest standard), property deed, or a hosting declaration from a Portuguese resident with proof of their own accommodation. Short-term bookings are sometimes accepted for the remote-work visa but may be questioned.

documents.name: Travel/health insurance valid in Portugal
documents.description: Policy covering medical expenses, urgent care and repatriation in Portugal for the whole visa validity (commonly minimum EUR 30,000 cover). Policies issued by Russian insurers are frequently rejected because of payment/sanctions issues — an international or EU-issued policy is safer.

documents.name: Portuguese tax identification number (NIF)
documents.description: Issued by the Portuguese Tax Authority; obtainable before departure through a fiscal representative or in Portugal at a Finanças office / Loja do Cidadão with passport and proof of address. Needed to sign a lease, open a bank account and complete the residence permit application.
documents.source: Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Portal das Finanças)

documents.name: Flight reservation showing arrival in Portugal
documents.description: One-way ticket or itinerary confirming the intended entry date; a return ticket is not required for national visas, but Russian applicants should note there are no direct flights and should show the actual routing used. Some centres list this as optional.

documents.name: Visa fee and BLS service fee payment receipt
documents.description: Proof of payment of the national visa consular fee (EUR 110 at the Moscow post) plus the separate BLS International service charge, paid at the visa application centre.

documents.name: AIMA residence permit appointment confirmation
documents.description: Some residence visas are issued with a pre-scheduled AIMA appointment printed on or attached to the visa; if not, the appointment must be requested through AIMA's online channel immediately after arrival and held within the visa's 120-day validity.

documents.name: Portuguese bank account confirmation with transferred funds
documents.description: Account opening declaration/IBAN and a statement showing the subsistence funds available locally, presented at the AIMA appointment. Russian citizens should expect enhanced compliance checks on the source of funds and on transfers originating from Russian banks.

documents.name: Updated income evidence for the AIMA appointment
documents.description: Recent payslips, invoices or client contracts dated after the visa was issued, proving the remote activity and income are still ongoing; presented together with the original consular file and the passport bearing the visa sticker.

documents.name: Portuguese social security number (NISS)
documents.description: Registration with Instituto da Segurança Social, required for self-employed/freelance remote workers who register an activity in Portugal, and often requested as supporting proof at AIMA where applicable.

documents.name: Residence permit card (Título de Residência) and SNS/address registration
documents.description: Card issued for 2 years and renewable for 3 years after biometrics at AIMA; on receipt, update the NIF address with Finanças and register at the local Centro de Saúde for the national health service. Absences above 6 consecutive or 8 non-consecutive months during the permit's validity jeopardise renewal and the 5-year path to permanent residence/citizenship.

documents.name: Valid Russian internal passport (общегражданский паспорт РФ)
documents.description: Russian citizens may cross into Armenia on the internal Russian passport under the CIS/bilateral regime; note it is accepted for air arrivals in practice, so an international passport is safer for land/mixed routes and for onward travel. If you enter on the internal passport, a notarized Armenian translation of it will later be demanded by almost every Armenian authority.
documents.source: Migration and Citizenship Service of Armenia (migration.mia.gov.am)

documents.name: Valid Russian international passport (загранпаспорт)
documents.description: Preferred travel document: no visa is needed for Russian citizens, and entry is granted on presentation of the passport alone. Recommended validity of at least 6 months remaining; it is also the document banks, notaries and the Migration Service work with most easily. Verify current validity expectations with the border service, as practice may differ by crossing point.
documents.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia (mfa.am)

documents.name: Proof of accommodation for the first stay
documents.description: Hotel booking or landlord/host details covering the initial days. Border officers may ask where you will stay; the same address is later reused for address registration, so obtain the host's or owner's contact data in writing.
documents.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia (mfa.am)

documents.name: Proof of sufficient funds / onward travel evidence
documents.description: Bank statement, card, cash or a return/onward ticket. Not a formal visa-free condition, but border officials may request it at their discretion — verify with the Armenian border service as practice varies by crossing point.
documents.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia (mfa.am)

documents.name: Russian birth certificates of accompanying children
documents.description: Originals for each minor travelling with you. Needed later for the child's Public Services Number and for school enrolment; if you entered on internal passports, the birth certificate must also be translated into Armenian and notarized.
documents.source: Migration and Citizenship Service of Armenia (migration.mia.gov.am)

documents.name: Russian marriage certificate (original, with apostille)
documents.description: Required only if you will apply for family-based residence status or register a spouse/family member on a residence application. Armenian authorities require civil-status documents to be apostilled and translated into Armenian, so obtain the apostille in Russia before departure.
documents.source: Migration and Citizenship Service of Armenia (migration.mia.gov.am)

documents.name: Russian criminal record certificate (справка о несудимости) with apostille
documents.description: A home-country police clearance is commonly requested in residence-status files and for some regulated employment; it cannot be obtained conveniently from abroad, so request it with apostille before leaving. Note: it is not on the core statutory list for every residence ground — verify against the Migration and Citizenship Service checklist for your specific ground.
documents.source: Migration and Citizenship Service of Armenia (migration.mia.gov.am)

documents.name: Passport entry stamp / border crossing record
documents.description: The stamp placed in your document at the border is your proof of legal entry and start date of the visa-free period; Russian citizens may generally stay up to 180 days within one year. Check the date and duration on the stamp immediately, as overstay leads to fines and possible entry bans, and the stamp is required when applying for a Public Services Number.
documents.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Armenia (mfa.am)

documents.name: Notarized Armenian translation of your Russian passport
documents.description: A translation of the exact document you entered on, certified by an Armenian notary. Explicitly required from Russian citizens for address registration, and required for the Public Services Number if you crossed the border on the internal passport.

documents.name: Notarized residential lease agreement
documents.description: A lease for your Armenian home, notarized (and ideally cadastre-registered), naming you as tenant. It is the standard proof of housing for address registration and is distinct from the owner's consent document.

documents.name: Property owner's consent plus copy of the owner's passport
documents.description: Written consent from the landlord (notarized if the owner cannot attend in person, and from all co-owners if the property is jointly owned), naming the persons to be registered, together with a copy of the owner's identity document.

documents.name: Address registration (grantsoum) application and state fee receipt
documents.description: Filed at the territorial Passport and Visa Department / Migration and Citizenship Service, usually via appointment through the Hartak or migration.e-gov.am portal; state fee around 1,000 AMD. For Russian citizens staying under 180 days in a calendar year, address registration alone can legalise presence for work purposes without a residence card.

documents.name: Police certificate confirming actual residence at the address
documents.description: Where housing documents are incomplete or occupancy is doubted, the police verify actual residence at the declared address within about 5 working days and issue a confirmation that closes the registration file.

documents.name: Public Services Number (PSN/SSN) certificate
documents.description: A 10-digit identifier issued to foreigners legally present in Armenia, obtained in person at a Migration and Citizenship Service subdivision or online with strong authentication; for foreigners it is issued as a stamped paper certificate rather than a card. Needed for employment, banking, taxes and public services, and a certificate of lawful residence cannot be printed without it.

documents.name: Armenian bank account opening file
documents.description: Bank onboarding typically requires the passport, the Public Services Number and proof of your Armenian address; banks generally ask for the PSN as part of identification, so obtain it first. Exact document lists differ by bank — confirm directly with the chosen bank.

documents.name: Employment contract with an Armenian employer
documents.description: As an EAEU national you are exempt from a work permit, but a signed employment agreement is the substantive basis for the certificate of lawful residence and for payroll/tax registration by the employer.

documents.name: Certificate confirming the legality of stay (EAEU certificate)
documents.description: The EAEU alternative to a work permit for Russian citizens working in Armenia beyond the short-stay period: the employee applies through the EAEU section of workpermit.am (the employer must first be registered on the platform). Application items include the PSN, passport copy, employment agreement, Armenian residence address and a 35x45 mm photo; it is normally issued for the contract term or one year.

documents.name: Temporary residence status application file (1-year residence card)
documents.description: Filed in person by appointment at the Migration and Citizenship Service, 14 Tairov Street, Yerevan, for grounds such as study, business, family or Armenian descent; the card is issued for up to one year and is renewable. Core file: application form, passport with notarized Armenian translation, photos, health certificate, proof of legal stay and evidence of the chosen ground; state fee reported at AMD 105,000 — confirm the current fee and checklist with the Service, and note that procedures move to the digital permits.am system under the reform effective 1 November 2026.

documents.name: Biometric photographs, 35x45 mm
documents.description: Recent colour passport-style photos (three copies are typically requested for a temporary residence file, one for the EAEU certificate application). These are separate from passport photocopies and must meet the size specification.

documents.name: Medical/health certificate for the residence file
documents.description: A health certificate on the form accepted by the Migration and Citizenship Service, normally issued by an Armenian clinic after arrival. A missing or wrongly formatted medical form is a frequent cause of delay — confirm the accepted issuing institutions with the Service.

documents.name: Residence status renewal or replacement application
documents.description: Renewal must be filed roughly 30 days before the card expires; a lost card can be restored and a card must be replaced if it becomes unusable or if you change your passport, by applying in person or via a representative at 14 Tairov Street.

documents.name: Valid Russian international passport (original)
documents.description: Russian biometric passport, valid well beyond the intended stay (Migration Department document lists require validity of at least 3 months beyond the permit period; Cyprus consulates in Russia generally ask for 6 months' validity beyond visa expiry and 2 blank pages). Both original and a full photocopy of all pages are submitted with the residence permit application.

documents.name: Cyprus entry visa issued by a Cypriot mission in Russia
documents.description: Russian nationals are not visa-exempt for Cyprus and must obtain a paper entry visa (short-stay/tourist or national visa) before travel; Cyprus is outside Schengen and issues its own visa. The Digital Nomad residence permit application is then filed inside Cyprus after lawful entry. Apply at the Embassy of the Republic of Cyprus in Moscow or a Cypriot Consulate General (St Petersburg, Yekaterinburg, Samara, Krasnodar) — confirm current appointment procedure and accepted visa category directly with the mission, as availability for Russian applicants has changed since 2022.
documents.source: Embassy of the Republic of Cyprus in Moscow (Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Cyprus)

documents.name: Russian criminal record certificate (справка об отсутствии судимости) from the MVD
documents.description: Original clean criminal record certificate issued by the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation (via MVD/Gosuslugi), normally not older than 6 months at submission. If you have also lived in a third country, a police certificate from that country of residence is expected as well.
documents.source: Ministry of Internal Affairs of the Russian Federation (MVD) / https://www.gov.cy/mip-md/en/documents/digital-nomads-and-family-members/

documents.name: Apostille and certified Greek/English translation of Russian-issued documents
documents.description: All documents accompanying the application must be officially translated (into Greek or English) and duly certified/ratified. Russia is a Hague Apostille Convention party, so the MVD police certificate, civil status certificates and medical documents should carry an apostille before translation; translations should be certified by a recognised/sworn translator (in Cyprus, the Press and Information Office register).

documents.name: Proof of remote work for a non-Cypriot employer or clients
documents.description: Employment contract with a company registered abroad, or — for self-employed applicants — service/project contracts with foreign clients plus company registration documents. The application form must state whether you are employed or self-employed, and the work must be performed via telecommunications technology for entities outside Cyprus.

documents.name: Bank statements and salary evidence proving €3,500+ net monthly income
documents.description: Statements covering roughly the last 6 months (plus payslips or invoices) showing stable net income of at least €3,500 per month after taxes and contributions; the threshold rises by 20% for a spouse/civil partner and 15% per child. Russian-bank statements should be translated and certified; consider also statements from a non-sanctioned foreign bank, as Cypriot banks and the Migration Department may query Russian-sourced funds (verify with the Department, practice varies by case officer).

documents.name: Private health insurance policy valid in Cyprus
documents.description: Accident and health insurance certificate covering inpatient and outpatient care and other medical expenses (repatriation cover is commonly requested) for the whole permit period. Check that the insurer's policy is accepted in Cyprus and is not limited by sanctions restrictions applying to Russian-issued policies.

documents.name: Original blood test results (HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and C)
documents.description: Original laboratory results certifying the applicant and dependants are free of these infectious diseases; results obtained abroad must be duly certified/legalised (apostille) and can alternatively be taken in Cyprus at a state or approved private lab after arrival. Children under 6 are exempt.

documents.name: Chest X-ray report for tuberculosis screening
documents.description: Original chest X-ray/radiology report certified by a physician, issued in the country of origin or last country of lawful residence (Russia) with proper certification, or performed in Cyprus after arrival. Children under 6 are exempt.

documents.name: Two recent biometric-standard photographs of the applicant
documents.description: Two colour passport-style photos (35x45 mm, plain background, no headgear/sunglasses) attached to the residence permit application form — separate from the digital photograph captured at the biometrics appointment and separate from passport photocopies.

documents.name: Apostilled Russian marriage certificate and children's birth certificates
documents.description: Needed only if a spouse/civil partner or minor children apply as family members; Russian ZAGS-issued certificates must be apostilled and translated into Greek or English. Family members file their own permit applications and cannot work or carry out economic activity in Cyprus.

documents.name: Completed Digital Nomad residence permit application form (MVIS4; MVIS6 for family members)
documents.description: Signed Migration Department form for the temporary residence permit, filed in person (or via authorised representative) at the Civil Registry and Migration Department central offices in Nicosia within 3 months of arrival, together with the fees of €70 for the permit and €70 for first registration in the Aliens Registry per person. Incomplete files are not processed; confirm the current form version/appointment need on the Department's website.

documents.name: Proof of accommodation in Cyprus (rental agreement or title deed)
documents.description: Signed long-term rental contract for the Cypriot address (landlord's title/ownership evidence is often attached), or the title deed if you own property; short-term booking confirmations are sometimes accepted for the initial filing — verify acceptability with the Migration Department.

documents.name: Photocopy of the passport page showing the last entry stamp into Cyprus
documents.description: Copy of the passport page(s) with the Cyprus entry visa and the most recent entry stamp, evidencing lawful entry and that the application is filed within the 3-month window (distinct from the general full-passport photocopy).

documents.name: Biometric data enrolment (fingerprints and digital photograph)
documents.description: Mandatory in-person capture of fingerprints and a facial image at the Migration Department in Nicosia or at an Aliens and Immigration Office of the Cyprus Police; the residence permit card cannot be issued without it. Children under six provide only a photograph.

documents.name: Signed affirmation that accompanying family members will not engage in economic activity
documents.description: Written declaration submitted with the family members' applications confirming they will not be employed or run a business in Cyprus while holding the dependent permit.

documents.name: Digital Nomad temporary residence permit card
documents.description: The issued permit (valid one year, renewable up to a total of three years) is your proof of legal residence in Cyprus; carry it with your passport. The permit is cancelled if you stay outside Cyprus for more than 90 consecutive days — plan absences accordingly.

documents.name: Alien Registration Certificate (ARC) / Aliens Registry registration
documents.description: First-time registration in the Aliens Registry (fee €70 per person, paid with the application) produces your alien registration number/certificate, routinely requested by Cypriot banks, insurers and utility providers.

documents.name: Cyprus Tax Identification Code (TIC) registration
documents.description: Register with the Cyprus Tax Department if you become a Cyprus tax resident — mainly under the 183-day rule — and file annual returns; a TIC is also frequently required for banking and GHS (GeSY) contributions. Russian tax residency status and the Russia–Cyprus double tax treaty position should be checked with a qualified adviser.

documents.name: Renewal application file with refreshed supporting evidence
documents.description: Submitted to the Civil Registry and Migration Department in Nicosia at least one month before the current permit expires, with updated proof of income at the €3,500+ threshold, a current remote-work contract, a valid insurance policy, current accommodation proof and the applicable fees; a fresh MVD criminal record certificate may be requested — verify the current renewal document list with the Department.

documents.name: Biometric passport of the Russian Federation
documents.description: Valid Russian biometric (chip) travel document — since 3 July 2024 Czechia recognises ONLY biometric passports issued by the Russian Federation; non-biometric Russian passports are not accepted for visa/residence permit applications. Must be issued within the last 10 years, contain at least 2 blank pages and be valid at least 3 months beyond the requested permit validity.

documents.name: Completed long-term residence permit application form (Žádost o povolení k dlouhodobému pobytu)
documents.description: Official bilingual Czech/English MFA form, one form per applicant, filled in legible Latin capitals and signed. First-time applications must be lodged in person at a Czech diplomatic mission competent for Russian citizens (territorial consular competence applies; Russians must generally apply at the mission in the state of citizenship or of long-term residence of 2+ years).

documents.name: Biometric-standard photographs of the applicant (3.5 x 4.5 cm)
documents.description: Printed passport-style photographs on light background, no head covering except for religious reasons, matching current appearance. Consulates commonly request 2–3 prints — verify the exact number with the specific Czech embassy/consulate handling your file.
documents.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic (mzv.gov.cz)

documents.name: Document proving the purpose of stay
documents.description: Original document matching the exact purpose of the long-term residence permit applied for (e.g. employment contract / employee card job offer, confirmation of enrolment at an accredited Czech university, family reunification documents, business registration, scientific research hosting agreement). A long-term residence permit is always issued for one specific purpose and that purpose must continue to exist.

documents.name: Proof of secured accommodation in the Czech Republic
documents.description: Lease agreement, accommodation confirmation from the property owner with notarised signature, or dormitory confirmation, covering the requested residence period at a specific Czech address.

documents.name: Proof of sufficient financial means
documents.description: Bank statements, Czech bank account confirmation, salary/scholarship confirmation or an internationally usable payment card together with an account balance statement. For study purposes the indicative annual amount is roughly CZK 125,000; thresholds differ by purpose — confirm the current figure for your purpose with the Ministry of the Interior.

documents.name: Russian criminal record extract (справка о наличии/отсутствии судимости) with Apostille
documents.description: Certificate of no criminal record issued by the Russian MVD. As a foreign public document it must carry higher verification — Russia is an Apostille Convention party, so an Apostille is required. Must not be older than 180 days at submission.

documents.name: Criminal record certificate(s) from other countries of residence in the last 3 years
documents.description: Equivalent document from any state where you resided continuously for more than 6 months during the past 3 years (relevant for Russian nationals who relocated via third countries such as Armenia, Kazakhstan, Serbia, Turkey or UAE), also apostilled/superlegalised.

documents.name: Certified Czech translations of all Russian-language documents
documents.description: Every Russian-issued document (criminal record extract, birth/marriage certificate, diplomas, employer letters) must be submitted with a translation into Czech; translations should be made by a court-appointed (soudní) translator. Translation of a document does not remove the separate Apostille requirement.

documents.name: Written justification for the application under Czech restrictive measures against Russian nationals
documents.description: Because Czechia applies restrictive visa measures in response to the aggression against Ukraine and, with limited exceptions, does not issue visas or residence permits to Russian nationals located outside the Czech Republic, Russian applicants should be prepared to document that they fall within an exemption (e.g. family reunification with a Czech resident, humanitarian grounds, or an application filed from within Czechia as a current permit holder). Not a standard statutory form — verify eligibility with the competent Czech embassy or the Ministry of the Interior before paying fees.

documents.name: Proof of paid administrative/consular fee
documents.description: Receipt for the application fee. Applications filed inside the Czech Republic cost CZK 2,500 (CZK 1,000 for persons under 15) and can only be paid by card at a Ministry of the Interior office; fees for applications filed at a diplomatic mission differ and must be confirmed with that mission (e.g. CZK 5,000 for a Blue Card).

documents.name: Czech medical insurance policy for presentation before the visa sticker is issued
documents.description: Once the Ministry of the Interior approves the permit, insurance covering the territory of the Czech Republic must be arranged and shown to the embassy before the entry visa is stamped into the passport. The embassy sends the specific policy parameters to each successful applicant.

documents.name: D/VR entry visa for collection of the residence permit
documents.description: Special long-stay visa sticker affixed in the passport by the Czech embassy after approval; it is not the residence permit itself but the entry document allowing you to travel to Czechia and collect the biometric card.

documents.name: Registration of arrival at a Ministry of the Interior office
documents.description: Holders of a D/VR visa must register at the competent Ministry of the Interior office within 30 calendar days of arrival; at registration the office schedules the biometric appointment and applies for your Czech personal identity (birth) number. If you enter legally by another route, the deadline is 3 days.

documents.name: Foreign Police residence registration form
documents.description: Separate obligation to report your Czech place of residence to the Department of Foreign Police within 3 days of entry; it does not apply if your accommodation provider (hotel, hostel, dormitory) reports you, or if you register your arrival at the Ministry of the Interior when collecting a long-term permit.

documents.name: Biometric data capture record (facial image and fingerprints)
documents.description: Attend the scheduled appointment with your passport to have your facial record and fingerprints scanned for the residence permit card; at this appointment you agree the collection date for the finished card.

documents.name: Biometric residence permit card (průkaz o povolení k pobytu)
documents.description: The actual long-term residence permit document, collected in person at the Ministry of the Interior within 60 days of the biometric data scan; it is the identity document you must present to police on request.

documents.name: Employer confirmation of commencement of work (employment-based permits only)
documents.description: When collecting a first employee card you must present the employer's confirmation, on the Ministry's form, that you have started work in the position for which the card was issued. Not applicable to study, family or research purposes.

documents.name: Notifications of changed personal or document data
documents.description: Written report to the Ministry of the Interior within 3 working days of any change of name, surname, marital status, travel document data (including issuance of a new Russian biometric passport) or data in your residence permit. Relevant for Russian citizens who must replace non-biometric passports.

documents.name: Application for extension of the long-term residence permit
documents.description: Must be filed in person at a Ministry of the Interior office no later than the last day of validity of your current permit or long-term visa (normally within the 120-day window before expiry); supporting documents must again be no older than 180 days. Russian nationals with pending extensions have in the past faced travel restrictions and 'bridge visa' limitations — verify current practice with the Ministry of the Interior.

documents.name: Czech language examination certificate (level A2) for later permanent residence
documents.description: Needed only when converting long-term residence into permanent residence after the required period of continuous residence; note that since 1 January 2025 Russian citizens may apply for Czech nationality only if they prove renunciation of Russian citizenship. Confirm the current exam level and residence period with the Ministry of the Interior.
documents.source: Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic

documents.name: Russian international passport (zagranpasport) valid 3+ months beyond planned departure
documents.description: Valid foreign travel document is the core identity document for entry and for the residence application. Montenegrin law considers a travel document valid if issued within the last ten years and not expiring earlier than three months after the planned date of departure from Montenegro. Bring the original; MUP also takes an uncertified photocopy of the passport's first (bio-data) page as a separate file item.

documents.name: Montenegrin long-stay (Type D) visa for Russian citizens
documents.description: Montenegro's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced that nationals of Russia (along with Belarus, China, Saudi Arabia and Türkiye) require a visa to enter Montenegro as of 1 November 2026; before that date Russian citizens could enter visa-free for up to 30 days. For a stay longer than 90 days the Type D long-stay visa is the entry route, applied for at a Montenegrin diplomatic mission/partner visa centre before departure. Exact start date and submission channel changed during 2026 — verify with the Montenegrin Ministry of Foreign Affairs or the Embassy in Moscow before booking travel.
documents.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Montenegro (MVP) / Embassy of Montenegro in Moscow

documents.name: Russian criminal-record certificate (справка о наличии (отсутствии) судимости) with Montenegrin court translation
documents.description: Certificate of no criminal record issued by the Russian MVD, typically not older than 6 months, translated into Montenegrin by a licensed court interpreter. Note: legalisation practice differs by source — some Montenegrin practitioners state that under the bilateral legal-assistance treaty Russian citizens do not need an apostille, while other guidance says long-stay files are routinely apostilled. Confirm apostille need with the specific MUP branch or consulate handling your file before ordering the certificate.

documents.name: Evidence justifying the legal ground of temporary residence
documents.description: Montenegro grants temporary residence only for a specific statutory purpose. Under the official framework, temporary residence can be approved for grounds such as family reunification, education, youth exchange, training, research, medical treatment, humanitarian reasons, ownership/use of real estate, religious service and work. With the application the foreigner must enclose all evidence justifying the reason for the request, and the ground cannot be changed while the decision is pending — so identify your ground (e.g. employer's written job offer, land-registry extract, university enrolment) before starting.

documents.name: Recognition (nostrification) decision for Russian diploma / education certificate
documents.description: For the employment-based route the Employment Agency's document list includes proof of attained education level and qualification — a nostrified diploma, i.e. the decision recognising the foreign educational qualification, or the foreign diploma together with confirmation that a recognition request has been submitted. Order the Russian diploma copy and translation before departure as recognition takes time.

documents.name: Russian birth certificate (and marriage certificate) with court translation
documents.description: Civil-status records are requested in practice when submitting a residence file, particularly for family reunification, for registering family members, and for the personal-data entries in the foreigner's ID card. Certified Montenegrin translation is required. Family-reunification applicants should also carry children's birth certificates.

documents.name: Biometric passport photographs (35 x 45 mm) of the applicant
documents.description: Colour photographs to the standard consular/ID format are needed for the long-stay visa application at the consulate, and a photograph is taken/used for the foreigner's ID card, whose photo field measures 24 x 33 mm. This is distinct from photocopies of the passport.

documents.name: Proof of financial means for the stay
documents.description: Evidence of sufficient funds to support living costs during the permit period. For the real-estate ground, practitioners cite a statement from a Montenegrin bank showing roughly €3,650 for a one-year permit (about €10 per day of stay); for the employment ground, since 2022 an employer's offer stating at least the minimum wage is accepted as proof of means instead of separate bank/salary evidence. Amounts and acceptable formats vary by ground — verify with MUP as figures are periodically revised.

documents.name: Health insurance valid in Montenegro for the permit period
documents.description: Proof of enrolment in a health insurance programme is part of the standard document list; the insurance must cover the full period of the requested permit. At the first-application stage a 30-day travel health policy or a certified Montenegrin health booklet is accepted in some procedures.

documents.name: Registration of address / stay (prijava boravišta – 'white card')
documents.description: Registration of the place of stay with the local MUP/police unit is the explicit first step in the official document sequence for a temporary residence and work permit; hotels register guests automatically, but in private accommodation the applicant or landlord must register the address, and the resulting registration slip is needed for the residence file. Register immediately after arrival.

documents.name: Proof of secured accommodation in Montenegro
documents.description: A lease/tenancy agreement (podstanarski ugovor) or a land-registry extract (list nepokretnosti) proving where you will live. For the real-estate ground the property must be registered in the cadastre (Katastar) in your name and free of unresolved legal issues; undeveloped land alone does not qualify.

documents.name: Temporary residence application submitted in person to MUP
documents.description: The application must be submitted in person to the Ministry at the applicant's place of residence, on the prescribed form provided by the police administration / Ministry of Interior; a first application may alternatively be lodged at a Montenegrin diplomatic or consular mission abroad. An applicant who files a complete application before 90 days of stay expire may remain in Montenegro until the final decision.

documents.name: Administrative fee payment receipts
documents.description: Receipts for state and local administrative charges must be in the file; the official Employment Agency list specifies a payment to giro account 825-50-71, model 05, with a reference number depending on the issuing municipality. Amounts and account references change — confirm the current figures at the MUP counter before paying.

documents.name: Biometric data enrolment at MUP
documents.description: At the MUP office the applicant is photographed and submits biometric data together with the personal documents; applicants may additionally be summoned for an interview about the purpose of immigration, previous employment or business plans.

documents.name: Temporary residence approval stamp in the passport / decision (rješenje)
documents.description: Approval of temporary residence is entered into the valid travel document by affixing a stamp headed 'Crna Gora' and 'ODOBRENJE PRIVREMENOG BORAVKA', with fields for the purpose of stay, validity period and the authorised officer's signature. Keep this decision — it is the legal basis for issuing your residence card.
documents.source: Pravilnik o načinu odobravanja privremenog boravka i stalnog nastanjenja (gov.me)

documents.name: Foreigner's ID card (lična karta za stranca)
documents.description: The polycarbonate card-format ID document (86 x 54 mm) issued to a foreigner after residence is approved; it is the day-to-day proof of your legal status in Montenegro and is applied for at MUP after the residence decision.
documents.source: Pravilnik o načinu odobravanja privremenog boravka i stalnog nastanjenja (gov.me)

documents.name: Employment contract and registration of employment with the Employment Agency
documents.description: For work-based residence, after temporary stay is approved the employer concludes the labour (or civil) contract with the foreigner and must register the employment with the Employment Service within 15 days of its start; the employer must also keep a copy of the residence-and-work permit at the workplace.

documents.name: Proof of paid taxes and social contributions (self-employed / executive directors)
documents.description: In a March 2026 interpretation, MUP confirmed that for entrepreneurs and executive directors who are sole owners or hold more than 51% of capital, evidence of paid tax and contribution obligations of at least €5,000 per year is one of the conditions for extending a temporary residence and work permit; the amended law entered into force on 17 January 2026 and the rule is not applied retroactively. Confirm applicability to your own company structure with MUP.

documents.name: Renewal application file for temporary residence
documents.description: The extension application must be submitted in person to the Ministry at the place of residence no later than 30 days before the current permit expires, accompanied by the valid travel document; in the official procedure no supporting document in the renewal file may be older than 6 months. If you leave Montenegro for more than one month in a year, notify your immigration inspector.

documents.name: Continuity-of-residence evidence for permanent residence (stalno nastanjenje)
documents.description: After five years of continuous temporary residence you may apply for permanent settlement; the official document list requires proof of approved continuous five-year residence in the form of copies of all passport pages bearing previous residence approvals, plus a certificate of no criminal record in Montenegro. Keep travel and address records tidy from year one.

documents.name: Valid Russian international passport (загранпаспорт)
documents.description: Machine-readable Russian international travel passport is the only entry document needed for visa-free entry; internal Russian passports are not accepted. Georgian practice expects validity covering the full intended stay, and official guidance advises validity of at least 3 months beyond planned departure (6 months is the safer margin recommended by many missions). Border officers have discretion where expiry is near.

documents.name: Health and accident insurance policy (min. 30,000 GEL coverage)
documents.description: Under the Law of Georgia 'On Tourism', since 1 January 2026 every tourist entering Georgia must hold a valid health and accident insurance policy, presented in paper or electronic form, in Georgian or English, issued by a Georgian or foreign insurer, with coverage of no less than 30,000 GEL and valid for the entire stay. Buy before departure; enforcement details and exemption categories should be verified on geoconsul.gov.ge as the rule is new.

documents.name: Proof of sufficient funds for the stay
documents.description: Border officers may request evidence of financial means: bank statements, a card with available balance, or a salary confirmation letter. Georgia publishes no fixed daily minimum, so the exact amount is at officer discretion — verify with the Consular Department of the MFA if travelling for an extended visa-free stay.
documents.source: Consular Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia (geoconsul.gov.ge)

documents.name: Proof of accommodation for arrival (hotel booking, lease, or notarized invitation)
documents.description: Georgian embassies advise holding accommodation details at border checkpoints: a hotel reservation, a lease agreement, or — if staying with a host — a notarized invitation letter on the MFA form. One document type is sufficient; this is separate from the later address-registration lease used for residency.

documents.name: Onward or return travel ticket
documents.description: Not a formal legal requirement for visa-free Russian nationals, but border officers frequently ask about departure plans; any confirmation of onward travel (flight, bus, or train booking) satisfies the question. Russian citizens should note that Russia–Georgia land crossings operate under special conditions, so route choice should be checked in advance.
documents.source: Consular Department, Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Georgia (geoconsul.gov.ge)

documents.name: Photocopies and digital scans of passport and insurance policy
documents.description: Keep paper photocopies plus cloud-stored scans of the passport bio-data page, insurance policy and accommodation confirmation, stored separately from the originals. This is a practical safeguard, not a legal entry requirement.

documents.name: Apostilled Russian civil-status documents (birth certificate, marriage certificate)
documents.description: Obtain apostilles from the Russian ZAGS/Ministry of Justice before leaving Russia if a family-based residence permit, family address registration, school enrolment or later citizenship application is possible. Georgian authorities require foreign-issued documents to be apostilled and translated into Georgian; certifications generally must not be older than six months at submission.

documents.name: Apostilled Russian educational diplomas and qualification certificates
documents.description: Needed only if a study-based or work-based residence permit, professional licensing, or recognition of Russian qualifications is planned. Apostille in Russia first — it is difficult to arrange from Georgia. Georgian translation will be required at submission.

documents.name: Apostilled and notarized power of attorney (optional, for representation)
documents.description: If a representative will register a company, an Individual Entrepreneur, or property on your behalf, the PoA must be notarized in Russia, apostilled and translated into Georgian; a PoA notarized inside Georgia is also possible once you are in the country.
documents.source: National Agency of Public Registry of Georgia (napr.gov.ge)

documents.name: Entry stamp / border-crossing record in passport
documents.description: The visa-free permission is granted automatically at the border, and the entry stamp is the proof of the legal-stay start date. Russian citizens currently receive up to one year (365 days) of visa-free stay; entry and exit dates are tracked automatically, and overstay leads to fines and possible entry bans. Confirm the exact allowed duration on the MFA visa-free list before travel, as some sources cite different periods.

documents.name: Rental agreement in the tenant's own name
documents.description: A written lease naming you as tenant is the practical foundation for address registration, bank onboarding and later residence-permit applications, and is stronger evidence than an informal arrangement. Keep the landlord's ownership extract details available.
documents.source: National Agency of Public Registry of Georgia (napr.gov.ge)

documents.name: Georgian taxpayer identification number (personal TIN) from the Revenue Service
documents.description: Foreign individuals who are not running a registered business are assigned a 9-digit TIN manually by the Revenue Service; registration can be done through the Revenue Service portal with video verification that must be completed from inside Georgia. Needed for tax filings, property purchase and some account openings.

documents.name: Georgian bank account opening file (passport plus source-of-funds evidence)
documents.description: Georgian banks apply enhanced due diligence to Russian citizens: expect to supply the international passport, a local address, and documentation of income/source of funds (employment contract, invoices, prior bank statements). Exact documentation varies by bank — confirm directly with the chosen bank, as this is a commercial rather than a state requirement.

documents.name: Individual Entrepreneur (IE) registration certificate with Entrepreneurs Registry
documents.description: Foreign nationals may register as an Individual Entrepreneur at the Public Service Hall via the National Agency of Public Registry using a valid international passport and a Georgian registration address; registration typically completes within one business day, followed by mandatory tax registration at rs.ge. Important: rules reported as effective from 1 March 2026 may require foreigners performing paid activity to hold a work/residence permit or D1 visa — verify current status with the Public Registry before relying on visa-free status alone.
documents.source: National Agency of Public Registry / Public Service Hall (psh.gov.ge)

documents.name: Small Business Status confirmation from the Revenue Service
documents.description: A separate application filed after IE registration to obtain the reduced turnover tax rate; approval depends on the business activity, as some activity types (including certain consulting work) are excluded. Filed with the Revenue Service of Georgia.

documents.name: Residence permit application form and supporting package (Public Service Hall)
documents.description: First-time residence permit applications must be filed from inside Georgia at a Public Service Hall / Public Service Development Agency, on the official form, with documents in Georgian (or accepted in another language at the Agency's discretion) and copies certified as prescribed by law. Grounds include work, study, family reunification, investment and property ownership, each with its own document list.

documents.name: Biometric photograph of the applicant for the residence file
documents.description: A recent colour photo (commonly 3x4 cm) is part of the residence permit package, and the applicant normally attends the Public Service Hall in person to be photographed for the card. This is distinct from the passport photocopies also submitted with the application.

documents.name: Evidence of legal income or bank balance for the residence permit
documents.description: Georgian regulation accepts an employment or business-activity document (labour contract or similar); where legal income is not confirmed that way, funds in the applicant's personal bank account may count, and the amount must be at least double the minimum subsistence level for average consumers, scaled to the permit duration. Work-permit applicants face additional thresholds, including an employer turnover requirement of 50,000 GEL per foreign employee (35,000 GEL for educational/medical institutions).

documents.name: Georgian residence card and address registration
documents.description: After a residence permit is granted, the holder must apply for a residence card at a Public Service Development Agency office, Public Service Hall branch or Community Centre within 30 days and register a living address; the card is the identity document certifying identity, citizenship and place of residence in Georgia.

documents.name: Residence permit renewal or permanent residence file
documents.description: Temporary permits are issued for 6-12 months initially and can be extended; renewals are normally submitted within a fixed window before expiry (roughly 40-90 days beforehand) and, unlike first applications, may be filed from abroad online. Permanent residence generally becomes available after several consecutive years on a temporary permit, or under a simplified property-based route. Confirm current renewal windows and qualifying periods with the Public Service Development Agency, as these rules have changed repeatedly.

documents.name: Russian Federation international passport (valid 60+ days beyond requested permit period)
documents.description: Ordinary Russian biometric passport used for entry. Official rule: applicants must hold a passport or passport-substitute document valid for at least sixty days longer than the requested residence permit period; an application cannot be finalised on an expired passport. Note that Russian ordinary-passport holders enter visa-free, but holders of official/special/service passports are not covered by the exemption and must obtain a visa before travel.

documents.name: Purpose-specific Turkish entry visa from a Turkish consulate in Russia (work / student cases only)
documents.description: If the residence permit basis is employment or study rather than tourism/property, the corresponding work or student visa must be obtained from a Turkish Embassy/Consulate in the Russian Federation before departure; the student visa is the basis of the later student residence permit. Not needed for applicants entering under the visa-free regime for tourism/property purposes.
documents.source: Republic of Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs / Turkish Consulate General in Russia

documents.name: Apostilled Russian criminal record certificate (справка о несудимости) with sworn Turkish translation
documents.description: Required for specific short-term categories, notably the investor basis, covering the last five years, and for long-term permit applications. Documents issued abroad must carry an apostille and a notarised Turkish translation; if not apostilled, consulate/Ministry of Foreign Affairs certification plus translation is accepted. Not requested for ordinary tourism-based short-term applications — verify with the provincial migration office, practice varies by province.

documents.name: Apostilled Russian civil-status certificates (birth certificate, marriage certificate) with notarised Turkish translation
documents.description: Needed for family-tie based applications and for accompanying minor children. Russian ZAGS-issued certificates must be apostilled and translated into Turkish by a sworn translator. If a child travels with only one parent, a certified consent of the absent parent is requested; certified custody or death certificates apply in divorce/widowhood cases.

documents.name: Proof of sufficient and regular income for the stay
documents.description: One of: pensioner identification card plus pension allocation certificate, bank statements showing the last three months of account movements, or a stamped and signed employer/company income document. Income documents obtained outside Türkiye must be translated into Turkish by a sworn translator. For short-term and student permits the foreigner's own declaration may be sufficient unless the administration specifically requests documents.

documents.name: Turkish potential tax identification number (Potansiyel Vergi Kimlik Numarası)
documents.description: Free 10-digit tax number for foreigners without a YKN, obtainable online from the Digital Tax Office with a scan of the passport photo page. Needed to pay residence permit fees, open a bank account, sign utility contracts and complete a property purchase before the ikamet card is issued.

documents.name: Signed printout of the e-ikamet residence permit application form
documents.description: The online application is completed at e-ikamet.goc.gov.tr, where the permit type is selected and a photo uploaded; the system then assigns an appointment at the provincial Directorate of Migration Management. The generated PDF must be printed, signed and brought to the appointment. The online application must be submitted before the visa-free stay or current permit expires.

documents.name: Four biometric photographs of the applicant
documents.description: Four recent passport-standard biometric photos taken against a white background, submitted in the application file. These are physical prints and are separate from the digital photo uploaded into the e-ikamet form.

documents.name: Photocopy of the passport plus notarised Turkish translation of passport pages
documents.description: Copies of the identity page, the last entry stamp page and the visa/e-visa page, with a notarised Turkish translation of the passport. This is a paper copy set for the file and is distinct from the original passport, which must also be presented on the appointment day.

documents.name: Valid private health insurance policy for foreigners covering the full permit period
documents.description: In principle insurance must cover the entire requested residence permit period; the first page of the policy is generally sufficient. Buying a policy for more than one year supports a longer permit. Alternatively, an official SGK application/provision document for General Health Insurance (GSS) is accepted where the applicant is covered by state insurance.

documents.name: Notarised Turkish residential lease agreement (noter tasdikli kira sözleşmesi)
documents.description: Proof of accommodation for tenants: a lease agreement notarised in Türkiye and containing the property owner's details. Important: new foreign address registration is closed or restricted in a large number of neighbourhoods and districts (including several in Istanbul), so confirm the specific address is open to new foreign registration before signing — verify with the local Directorate of Migration Management or Nüfus office.

documents.name: Title deed (Tapu) copy plus municipal numbering (numarataj) certificate — property-owner applicants
documents.description: For applicants basing a short-term permit on property ownership, the property must be registered in the applicant's name in the Turkish land registry; a title deed copy is submitted with a numbering certificate from the municipality on first application (and a title-deed continuation certificate on extension). A minimum declared property value threshold applies and has been raised in recent years — verify the current figure with the Presidency of Migration Management, as reported thresholds vary by source.

documents.name: Notarised host commitment letter (yabancı misafir taahhütnamesi) with host's residence certificate and utility bill
documents.description: Only for applicants staying at a third party's home instead of their own lease or property: a notarised undertaking by the accommodation provider (co-signed by the spouse if married), a current utility subscription/invoice in the host's name, and the host's residence certificate. Migration Management has significantly tightened acceptance of commitment-letter registrations, including occupancy-per-dwelling checks.

documents.name: Residence permit fee and card fee payment receipts
documents.description: After submitting the online form the system produces an accrual number (tahakkuk numarası); the residence permit fee and the card fee are paid against it and the receipts are added to the application file. Payment can be made online via the Digital Tax Office or in cash at a tax office depending on the fee type and province.

documents.name: Fingerprint registration at the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management
documents.description: Biometric fingerprints are taken at the migration office for first-time applicants. If a fingerprint number already appears on the documents of an extension or transfer applicant, new fingerprinting is not required.
documents.source: Presidency of Migration Management (Göç İdaresi Başkanlığı)

documents.name: Residence permit card (ikamet kartı) with Foreigner Identification Number (YKN)
documents.description: The physical card is dispatched from Ankara by PTT after approval; processing typically takes several weeks and varies by province. The card carries the 11-digit Yabancı Kimlik Numarası, which becomes the primary identifier for taxation, banking, property and utility transactions. If lost or stolen, file a police loss report and re-apply at the provincial migration office with the report, a biometric photo and address registration proof.

documents.name: Address registration and residence certificate (yerleşim yeri belgesi)
documents.description: Once the permit is approved, the address must be registered in the national address system. Since mid-2024 an appointment must first be booked through the Migration Management appointment system; walk-in manual registration was discontinued. The resulting residence certificate can afterwards be downloaded from e-Devlet and the entry checked in the National Address Query System using the YKN.

documents.name: UETS registered electronic notification address (Kayıtlı Elektronik Posta) from PTT
documents.description: A National Electronic Notification System address obtained in person at a PTT office. Required in extension and transfer residence permit applications (applicable from 15.04.2024); not required for applicants under 18.

documents.name: Separate work permit application (İŞKUR/Ministry of Labour) if employment is intended
documents.description: A residence permit does not itself grant the right to work. Foreigners intending to work must apply for a work permit under International Labour Force Law No. 6735, or for a work permit exemption under Article 48 of its implementing regulation. Income supporting a tourism-based short-term permit must come from outside Türkiye.

documents.name: Notification of change in personal circumstances to the Provincial Directorate of Migration Management
documents.description: Any change of name/surname, marital status, passport, address, employer, or school/programme must be reported to the provincial migration office immediately after it occurs, to keep the permit valid and avoid problems at renewal.
documents.source: Presidency of Migration Management (Göç İdaresi Başkanlığı)

documents.name: Russian international passport (zagranpasport)
documents.description: Original biometric Russian foreign-travel passport with at least 6 months validity beyond the intended entry date and blank pages for the entry stamp. Russian citizens enter the UAE visa-free for up to 90 days within any rolling 180-day period, which is the window normally used to complete freelance permit and residence formalities.

documents.name: Colour scan of passport bio-data page
documents.description: High-resolution digital scan/photocopy of the passport data page (plus any prior UAE visa pages) uploaded to the free zone or MOHRE online portal at application stage. This is a document upload, separate from presenting the original passport at the service centre.

documents.name: Biometric passport-style photograph of the applicant
documents.description: Recent colour photograph of the applicant, white background, full face, meeting UAE immigration specifications; needed digitally for the permit/visa application and physically at the medical and Emirates ID stages. Distinct from the passport scan.

documents.name: Freelance permit / sole professional licence application file
documents.description: Application for a freelance permit or sole-professional licence for an approved activity, submitted either to MOHRE (federal freelance work permit) or to a free zone authority (e.g. DDA/GoFreelance in Dubai, or a Northern Emirates free zone). Activity lists and availability change, so confirm your exact profession is currently open with the issuing authority before paying.

documents.name: University degree or specialised diploma with full Russian consular legalisation
documents.description: Original diploma legalised through the Russian chain — notarisation, Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication, then attestation at the UAE Embassy/Consulate in Moscow. A Hague apostille alone is not accepted because the UAE is not a party to the Apostille Convention; stages inside Russia must be completed before departure. Mandatory for the 5-year Green Visa freelancer track (bachelor's degree or equivalent minimum).

documents.name: Certified Arabic or English translation of Russian-language documents
documents.description: Sworn/notarised translation of Russian-issued documents (diploma, marriage and birth certificates, police record) into English or Arabic, as UAE missions and authorities do not accept Russian-only text. Have translations legalised together with the originals.
documents.source: UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFAIC) — consular legalisation requirements

documents.name: Proof of self-employment income for the previous two years
documents.description: Bank statements, audited accounts or certified income records showing annual self-employment income of at least AED 360,000 for each of the last two years — the threshold for the Green Visa freelancer/self-employed category.

documents.name: Proof of financial solvency for the residence period
documents.description: Alternative to the AED 360,000 income history: evidence of sufficient funds to support yourself throughout residency (bank balance certificates, liquid assets). Note that Russian-bank statements are frequently questioned by UAE banks and authorities; obtain stamped, translated statements and verify acceptance with the issuing authority.

documents.name: Client contracts, invoices or letters of engagement
documents.description: Signed service agreements or historic invoices evidencing independent professional activity in the requested field. Used by free zone authorities and MOHRE to justify the activity chosen and to corroborate declared freelance income.
documents.source: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE)

documents.name: Russian criminal record certificate (справка о несудимости), legalised
documents.description: Certificate of no criminal record from the Russian MVD, translated and consular-legalised. Not uniformly demanded for freelance permits but requested for some free zones, activities and long-term residence categories — verify with the specific issuing authority, requirements vary.
documents.source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

documents.name: UAE entry permit or visa-free entry stamp
documents.description: Either the 90-day visa-free entry stamp granted to Russian passport holders on arrival, or an employment/residence entry permit issued electronically once the freelance permit is approved. If already in the UAE on another residence visa, do not cancel it before the freelance/self-employment permit is issued.

documents.name: Issued freelance permit / licence certificate
documents.description: The final permit or sole-professional licence document naming you as the licensee in your own legal name. This is the work authorisation that lets you invoice UAE clients; it is separate from, and issued before, the residence visa.

documents.name: Establishment (immigration) card
documents.description: Immigration file/establishment card linked to your freelance licence, which is what allows the licence to sponsor your own residence visa and later your dependants. Issued by the licensing free zone together with the permit.

documents.name: MOFAIC attestation of the legalised Russian documents
documents.description: Final leg of the legalisation chain, performed inside the UAE by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on documents already attested at the UAE mission in Moscow. Required before the degree can be used for Green Visa or professional recognition.

documents.name: Medical fitness test certificate
documents.description: Result of the mandatory medical screening (chest X-ray and blood tests for communicable diseases) at a government-approved centre in the emirate of application. Must be completed in the UAE after the entry permit and before visa issuance.
documents.source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

documents.name: UAE health insurance policy
documents.description: Valid UAE-compliant medical insurance in your own name — compulsory for residence visa issuance as a self-sponsored freelancer, since there is no employer providing cover. Minimum plan requirements differ by emirate (e.g. DHA basic plan in Dubai).

documents.name: Emirates ID application and biometric enrolment
documents.description: ICP registration with fingerprints and facial capture; the Emirates ID card is the operative national identity document and its issuance activates your residency in practice.
documents.source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

documents.name: Residence visa (electronic residence permit)
documents.description: The residence permit itself, issued after medical, insurance and Emirates ID steps — either a 1–2 year visa sponsored by your freelance licence, or the 5-year Green Visa if you meet the permit, degree and income/solvency conditions.

documents.name: Registered tenancy contract (Ejari or emirate equivalent)
documents.description: Government-registered lease in your name, used as proof of address for banking, utilities, dependant sponsorship and visa renewal. Registration authority differs by emirate (Ejari via Dubai Land Department; equivalent Tawtheeq/municipality systems elsewhere).

documents.name: Federal Tax Authority registrations and Tax Residency Certificate
documents.description: Corporate tax registration and TRN for the licensed freelance activity, and — for Russian nationals needing to evidence a change of tax residence — a UAE Tax Residency Certificate issued by the Federal Tax Authority after meeting the physical-presence and residence conditions. Confirm current thresholds and small-business relief directly with the FTA.

documents.name: Russian international passport (original)
documents.description: Ordinary Russian Federation travel passport that must remain valid at least 6 months from the intended travel date; the DTV is issued for 5 years, so a passport with long remaining validity avoids having to transfer the visa to a new passport later.

documents.name: Scan/copy of the passport biodata page
documents.description: A separate colour copy or upload of the personal-data page of the Russian passport, submitted in addition to presenting the original passport. This is a distinct checklist item from the passport itself.

documents.name: Biometric photograph of the applicant
documents.description: One recent photo taken within the past 6 months, ICAO-standard: full-face, plain white background, no hat or tinted lenses. Uploaded as a digital file for the e-Visa application (not the same item as the passport copy).

documents.name: Completed DTV application submitted on the Thai e-Visa portal
documents.description: Online visa application form for the Destination Thailand Visa. Since 1 January 2025 all Royal Thai missions, including the Royal Thai Embassy in Moscow, process DTV applications through the mandatory e-Visa system; the application must be lodged while physically outside Thailand. The Russia-post fee is charged in USD (approx. 350 USD) rather than in THB.

documents.name: Bank statement showing 500,000 THB equivalent (3 months)
documents.description: Official bank statement for the last 3 months with an ending balance of no less than 500,000 THB equivalent (for Russian applicants, typically a RUB or foreign-currency account statement). Funds must be 'seasoned' — held for at least 3 months. Cryptocurrency wallets and brokerage/investment statements are generally not accepted; verify accepted bank formats with the Royal Thai Embassy in Moscow, as practice varies by mission.

documents.name: Proof of monthly income / salary slips for the last 6 months
documents.description: Payslips, remittance records or income statements covering 6 months, evidencing ongoing income from a source outside Thailand. This is a separate checklist item from the 500,000 THB balance statement.

documents.name: Foreign employment contract or employer certificate (Workcation category)
documents.description: Contract or letter of employment from a company registered outside Thailand. The MFA checklist requires it to be authenticated/legalised by the embassy of the country where the company is registered; for a Russian employer this normally means notarisation and legalisation in Russia. Verify the exact legalisation format with the Royal Thai Embassy in Moscow — requirements vary by consulate.

documents.name: Company registration / business licence of the non-Thai employer or own company
documents.description: Copy of the corporate registration extract or business licence of the foreign employer, or of your own registered company (e.g. Russian EGRUL/EGRIP extract for an IP or OOO), authenticated by the embassy of the country of registration. Applies to employees and to self-employed owners.

documents.name: Freelance evidence pack: client contracts and recent invoices
documents.description: For freelancers without a single employer: signed client contracts with non-Thai clients plus recent invoices/payment records. Since 2025 a CV or portfolio website alone is generally considered insufficient; documentary contracts are expected. Required only if you have no employment contract.

documents.name: Letter of acceptance from a Thai soft-power host organisation
documents.description: Alternative to the Workcation evidence: enrolment/acceptance letter from an accredited Muay Thai gym, Thai culinary school, sports or cultural programme, or a hospital letter for medical treatment. Programmes are generally expected to run at least 6 months; Thai language schools were removed from this category in 2025.

documents.name: Proof of your location/legal residence in the country of application
documents.description: Evidence that you are applying from outside Thailand and are legally present where you apply — e.g. Russian internal registration (propiska) or a utility bill if applying from Russia, or a residence permit/long-term visa if applying at a third-country mission such as Vientiane or Kuala Lumpur. Some missions refuse non-residents.

documents.name: Accommodation / long-stay evidence for Thailand
documents.description: Some Royal Thai missions ask for a condominium rental agreement, lease or equivalent showing intended prolonged stay in Thailand. This is not uniformly enforced — verify with the specific mission before applying, as requirements may vary by consulate.

documents.name: Certified English translations of Russian-language documents
documents.description: All supporting documents must be submitted in English or Thai. Russian-issued bank statements, employment contracts, company extracts and civil-status certificates therefore need certified/notarised English translations.

documents.name: Dependent relationship documents (marriage / birth certificate)
documents.description: For a spouse or unmarried children under 20 applying as dependents: Russian marriage certificate or birth certificate, translated and legalised, plus the primary applicant's passport biodata page and DTV visa/application reference. Dependents do not need to show separate 500,000 THB funds.

documents.name: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) submission
documents.description: Mandatory online arrival declaration replacing the paper TM6, completed within 72 hours before every arrival in Thailand by air, land or sea — including each re-entry on the 5-year multiple-entry DTV. Keep the TDAC reference number: it is needed for the online 90-day reporting system.

documents.name: Printed DTV e-Visa approval letter
documents.description: The approval issued by email as a PDF after e-Visa processing. Carry a printed copy for airline check-in in Russia/transit and for presentation to the Thai immigration officer at the border, since no visa sticker is placed in the passport under the e-Visa system.

documents.name: TM30 notification of residence (filed by the host/landlord)
documents.description: The house owner, condo juristic person or landlord must notify Thai Immigration of your address within 24 hours of your moving in; hotels file it automatically. Obtain and keep the TM30 receipt/screenshot — without it the immigration office can refuse your 90-day report or extension.

documents.name: TM47 90-day notification of residence
documents.description: Personal obligation under Section 37(5) of the Immigration Act for any foreigner staying more than 90 consecutive days on one permission of stay, which applies to DTV holders who do not leave. File in person, by registered post or online; window is 15 days before to 7 days after the due date. Late filing typically incurs a 2,000 THB fine. The counter resets only on re-entry to Thailand.

documents.name: TM7 application for extension of temporary stay
documents.description: Filed at the local immigration office to extend the 180-day DTV entry once by a further 180 days, fee 1,900 THB. Submitted with passport, photo, TM30 evidence and address proof. Note that extending does not reset the 90-day reporting counter.

documents.name: Certificate of Residence from Thai Immigration
documents.description: Immigration-issued residence certificate commonly requested by Thai banks for opening an account and by the Department of Land Transport for a Thai driving licence. Issued against passport, DTV entry stamp, TM30 and lease; availability and evidence required differ by immigration office — verify locally.

documents.name: Thai Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) application
documents.description: If you are physically present in Thailand for 180 days or more in a calendar year you become Thai tax-resident and may need to register with the Revenue Department and file a return on assessable income brought into Thailand. Russian applicants should also check the Russia–Thailand double taxation treaty; confirm your position with the Revenue Department or a tax adviser.

documents.name: Completed national visa application form (D8 residence visa)
