documents.name: Nigeria Police Force criminal record certificate
documents.description: Police clearance certificate covering Nigeria, plus one from any other country lived in for 12 months or more in the last 10 years. Required only for specified occupations (e.g. healthcare, education, roles working with children or vulnerable adults) — confirm applicability against the Home Office list before paying for it.

documents.name: Biometric enrolment confirmation from a Visa Application Centre (Lagos or Abuja) or ID Check app verification
documents.description: Either an appointment confirmation and biometric receipt after giving fingerprints and a facial image at the VFS/TLS visa application centre in Lagos or Abuja, or completed identity verification via the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app if eligible. This is distinct from any printed passport-style photographs a clinic or agent may request.

documents.name: Nigerian academic and professional qualification certificates
documents.description: Degree/diploma certificates and, where the role requires it, professional registration evidence (e.g. GMC, NMC, HCPC decision letter). Some sponsors and UKVI expect Nigerian certificates authenticated by the issuing institution and the Nigerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs — verify with the sponsor and UKVI, requirements vary by occupation.

documents.name: Dependant relationship documents (Nigerian marriage certificate and NPC birth certificates)
documents.description: Required only if a partner or children apply as dependants: Nigerian marriage certificate or evidence of 2 years' cohabitation, and National Population Commission birth certificates naming both parents. Each dependant also needs their own TB certificate and IHS payment.

documents.name: Visa decision letter and entry clearance (vignette or eVisa confirmation)
documents.description: The Home Office decision letter stating conditions of entry, plus the 90-day travel vignette in the passport where one is still issued. The UK has moved to digital status, so many applicants now travel on an eVisa alone — verify at collection whether a vignette was placed in your passport.

documents.name: UKVI account with eVisa access
documents.description: Free digital account created at gov.uk/get-access-evisa using your passport and GWF/UAN reference, verified with the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app. The eVisa has replaced the Biometric Residence Permit, biometric residence cards and passport endorsements as the record of status; passport details in the account must be kept current for carrier checks when travelling.

documents.name: Right-to-work share code (W code)
documents.description: Nine-character code beginning with 'W' generated in the 'View and prove your immigration status' service and given to the UK employer with your date of birth so they can complete the statutory right-to-work check. Valid 90 days; this is separate from the right-to-rent code.

documents.name: Right-to-rent share code (R code)
documents.description: Separate nine-character code beginning with 'R' generated from the same UKVI account, provided to a landlord or letting agent in England to evidence right to rent before signing a tenancy.

documents.name: National Insurance number
documents.description: Needed for PAYE payroll and social security contributions. Some work visa holders have an NI number issued with their immigration decision; if not shown in your eVisa or decision letter, apply through the HMRC/DWP online service after arrival.

documents.name: UK tenancy agreement or proof of address
documents.description: Signed assured shorthold tenancy agreement, or a letter/utility bill in your name, used to open a bank account, register with a GP and evidence residence. Keep the original — many banks will not accept a mobile phone bill.

documents.name: NHS GP registration (GMS1 form)
documents.description: Completed GMS1 registration form submitted to a local GP practice with your passport and proof of address to access NHS primary care already funded by your Immigration Health Surcharge.

documents.name: Record of absences from the UK
documents.description: A running log of every trip outside the UK with dates, supported by passport stamps and boarding passes. Settlement requires absences of no more than 180 days in any rolling 12-month period across the qualifying years, so this must be maintained from arrival.

documents.name: Life in the UK test pass notification
documents.description: Unique reference number issued after passing the Life in the UK test at an approved test centre; needed for indefinite leave to remain and later naturalisation. Book only through the official GOV.UK booking service.

documents.name: Indefinite Leave to Remain application pack (form SET(O)) with sponsor letter and salary evidence
documents.description: Online SET(O) settlement application supported by a current employer/sponsor letter confirming continued employment, payslips and P60s showing the applicable salary threshold is met at the application date, English language evidence and the Life in the UK result. Settlement rules are under reform ('earned settlement' proposals) — confirm the qualifying period and salary threshold on GOV.UK before applying.

documents.name: Nigerian international passport (machine-readable, valid)
documents.description: Standard Nigerian e-passport issued by the Nigeria Immigration Service. The biographic data page is uploaded in the e-APR, and the passport must remain valid through landing because the permanent resident visa counterfoil is affixed inside it. Renew early if validity is under 12 months.

documents.name: IRCC-approved language test result (IELTS General Training, CELPIP-General, PTE Core, TEF/TCF Canada)
documents.description: Test results must be less than two years old on the date the Express Entry profile is submitted and still valid when the e-APR is filed. Nigerian applicants most commonly use IELTS General Training at British Council/IDP centres in Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt or Ibadan. Academic IELTS is not accepted for Express Entry.

documents.name: Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) report
documents.description: Issued by an IRCC-designated organization (WES is the route most Nigerian applicants use). Nigerian university transcripts must be sent directly by the institution and WAEC/NECO secondary results are sent directly through the exam board's online verification service — allow several months for Nigerian institutional delays. ECA validity is five years from issue.

documents.name: Degree certificate, diploma and academic transcripts
documents.description: The underlying credentials themselves, uploaded separately from the ECA report. Include the final degree certificate/statement of result and full academic transcript for each credential claimed for CRS points.
documents.source: IRCC – Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada

documents.name: Employer reference letters for each period of skilled work experience
documents.description: On company letterhead, signed by someone with authority over your employment, stating job title, detailed duties, employment dates, hours per week, and salary/benefits, and matching the NOC code claimed. One letter per employer. For Nigerian employers that have closed or will not issue letters, substitute contracts, payslips, PAYE/tax records plus a written explanation.

documents.name: Nigeria Police Character Certificate (Police Clearance Certificate)
documents.description: Issued by the Nigeria Police Force Criminal Investigation Department at Force Headquarters, Alagbon Close, Lagos (INTERPOL/CRC route also used). Processing commonly takes 4–12 weeks, so start immediately after the Invitation to Apply. Must generally be issued within six months of e-APR submission; IRCC does not accept certificates mailed directly by the police to IRCC for Express Entry. Some applicants additionally have it authenticated by the Nigerian Ministry of Foreign Affairs or certified at a Nigerian mission abroad — verify with the official source, practice varies.

documents.name: Police certificates from every other country of residence (6+ months since age 18, last 10 years)
documents.description: Separate from the Nigerian certificate. Required for each country/territory other than Canada where you (and each accompanying family member 18+) lived six or more consecutive months in the past ten years — e.g. UK ACRO, US FBI Identity History Summary, UAE, Saudi Arabia, South Africa. If a certificate is delayed, upload documented proof of the request.

documents.name: Immigration medical examination (IME) report from an IRCC panel physician
documents.description: Must be done by a panel physician on IRCC's list (clinics in Lagos, Abuja, Port Harcourt and Benin City). Results are valid 12 months. An upfront exam before e-APR submission is optional but can shorten processing; the eMedical Information Sheet/IMM 1017 receipt is uploaded as proof.

documents.name: Biometrics enrolment (ten fingerprints and facial photograph) at a Canada VAC
documents.description: Distinct from the digital photo uploaded in your application. Biometrics must be given in person after receiving the Biometric Instruction Letter — in Nigeria at the VFS Global-operated Canada Visa Application Centre in Lagos or Abuja, by prior appointment. Every permanent residence applicant 14–79 must give biometrics again even if previously enrolled; the CAD 85 fee (CAD 170 per family) is paid with the application.

documents.name: Digital photograph meeting IRCC specifications (for the application and PR card)
documents.description: A separate uploaded photo file, not the biometric photo captured at the VAC. IRCC reuses the photo attached to your Confirmation of Permanent Residence to produce your first PR card, so it must meet the published size, framing and recency specifications.

documents.name: Proof of funds — official bank letter plus six months of account statements
documents.description: Required for Federal Skilled Worker and Federal Skilled Trades applicants without a valid Canadian job offer or existing Canadian work authorization; Canadian Experience Class applicants are exempt. The bank letter must be on letterhead with contact details, account numbers, opening dates and balances; IRCC assesses the whole six-month window, not a single snapshot, so unexplained large deposits should be documented. Nigerian applicants commonly hold funds in a USD domiciliary account to avoid naira valuation problems.

documents.name: Civil status records: birth certificate / attestation of birth, and marriage certificate or divorce decree
documents.description: Nigerian birth certificate from the National Population Commission (or a sworn declaration of age plus attestation of birth where no NPopC record exists) for you and each dependent child, plus marriage certificate for an accompanying spouse or final divorce/death certificate to establish current marital status. Customary/traditional marriages usually need the registry certificate or a court affidavit — verify with the official source.
documents.source: National Population Commission of Nigeria / IRCC

documents.name: Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR) and permanent resident visa counterfoil
documents.description: Issued on approval; the counterfoil is placed in your Nigerian passport at the visa office and both documents carry an expiry date tied to your medical exam. You must travel to Canada before that expiry. Keep the paper/e-COPR — it is your proof of status until the PR card arrives.
documents.source: IRCC – Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada

documents.name: CBSA landing examination: COPR, passport and Canadian mailing address
documents.description: At the port of entry a Canada Border Services Agency officer examines your valid passport and COPR and completes your landing. Give the officer a Canadian mailing address so PR card production starts automatically; if you have no address yet you may supply it to IRCC online within 180 days of becoming a permanent resident.

documents.name: Personal effects accounting document (BSF186) and Goods to Follow list (BSF186A)
documents.description: Two typed, valued inventories presented to CBSA at first landing — one for goods accompanying you, one for goods being shipped later. Settlers' effects enter duty- and tax-free only if listed at landing, so items still in Nigeria (household goods, vehicle) must appear on the Goods to Follow list.

documents.name: Currency/monetary instruments declaration for CAD 10,000 or more
documents.description: Cash, bank drafts, traveller's cheques or money orders totalling CAD 10,000 or more (in any currency combined) must be declared to CBSA on arrival. Undeclared funds can be seized. Carry the bank draft or transfer documentation for your settlement funds.

documents.name: Social Insurance Number (SIN)
documents.description: Applied for in person at a Service Canada centre (or online) with your COPR/e-COPR and passport; a permanent SIN is normally issued at the appointment with a confirmation-of-SIN letter. Required to work, be paid legally and receive federal benefits.

documents.name: Permanent Resident (PR) card
documents.description: Your first PR card is mailed automatically to a Canadian address — no application form is needed — provided you supplied the address and an acceptable photo within 180 days of landing. It must be delivered in Canada and is the document you need, together with your passport, to re-enter Canada on a commercial carrier.

documents.name: Provincial or territorial health insurance card
documents.description: Applied for through the health ministry of your province of residence using your COPR/PR card, photo ID and proof of a local address. Some provinces impose a waiting period before coverage begins (for example Ontario historically applied a three-month wait), so apply immediately on arrival and keep the application receipt.
documents.source: Provincial/territorial ministry of health (e.g. ServiceOntario, Alberta Health, Health Insurance BC)

documents.name: Provincial driver's licence with Nigerian driving history letter
documents.description: Nigeria has no reciprocal full-exchange agreement with Canadian provinces, so most Nigerian newcomers must complete provincial knowledge and road tests. A letter of driving experience from the Federal Road Safety Corps / state licensing authority, translated and sometimes authenticated, can reduce the graduated-licensing waiting period and insurance premiums — requirements differ by province, verify with the provincial licensing body.
documents.source: Provincial driver licensing authority (e.g. ServiceOntario, Alberta Registries, ICBC)

documents.name: Canada Revenue Agency tax records for your first filing year
documents.description: As a newcomer you file a first Canadian tax return for the year you landed, using your date of entry as your residency start date. Keep your T4 slips, COPR (date of landing) and records of foreign income and assets; filing is what unlocks GST/HST credit, Canada Child Benefit and later proof-of-residency evidence for citizenship.

documents.name: Residency-day evidence for maintaining PR status and future citizenship
documents.description: Retain boarding passes, passport entry/exit stamps, lease agreements, employment records and bank statements. Permanent residents must be physically present in Canada at least 730 days in every rolling five-year period to keep status, and 1,095 days in five years to apply for citizenship — this evidence is what proves it if questioned at a port of entry or on PR card renewal.

documents.name: Valid Philippine passport
documents.description: Original Philippine passport with at least 6 months' validity beyond the intended entry date; the passport data page is the base document for the freelance permit, entry permit and Emirates ID file. Name spelling must match all attested certificates exactly.
documents.source: Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA), Republic of the Philippines

documents.name: Recent biometric passport-size photographs of the applicant
documents.description: Colour photos with plain white background meeting UAE immigration specification (head-and-shoulders, no glasses/head covering unless religious). Used for the freelance licence file, entry permit and Emirates ID card — separate from any photocopies of the passport.
documents.source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

documents.name: Freelance permit / freelancer licence application with declared activity
documents.description: Online application to the chosen issuing authority (e.g. Dubai Development Authority / GoFreelance-TECOM, twofour54 Abu Dhabi, RAKEZ, Ajman FZ, UAQ FTZ) selecting one or more approved freelance activities from that authority's activity list. Some Dubai activity packages have been temporarily restricted — verify current availability directly with the issuing free zone.

documents.name: Attested Philippine degree/diploma (CHED CAV → DFA Apostille → UAE Embassy Manila)
documents.description: Educational certificate authenticated by the Commission on Higher Education (sealed CAV envelope — do not open), then apostilled by DFA Manila, then attested by the UAE Embassy in Manila. The UAE is not a Hague Apostille state for incoming documents, so the DFA apostille alone is not accepted.
documents.source: Commission on Higher Education (CHED), Philippines / UAE Embassy in Manila

documents.name: Professional portfolio or experience/qualification evidence
documents.description: Work samples, client references or CV proving competence in the declared freelance activity. Mandatory for regulated activities (e.g. personal trainer, media, education roles) and optional for others — confirm the exact evidence list with your issuing free zone.

documents.name: Personal bank statements / certified income records
documents.description: Statements (typically 6 months for a standard freelance residence visa; around 24 months of income records plus AED 15,000+ average monthly income if applying for the self-sponsored 5-year Green Visa as a freelancer). Philippine-issued statements should be in English or officially translated.
documents.source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

documents.name: NBI clearance (Philippine police clearance) with DFA apostille
documents.description: Good-conduct certificate issued by the National Bureau of Investigation, apostilled by DFA and — if the UAE authority requests it — attested by the UAE Embassy in Manila. Not demanded by every freelance-permit issuer; verify with the specific free zone, requirements vary by authority and activity.

documents.name: DMW exit clearance — OFW Travel Pass (formerly OEC)
documents.description: Philippine departure clearance for nationals leaving to work abroad, generated digitally via the eGovPH/DMW app once employment or engagement is verified; it replaces the printed Overseas Employment Certificate and gives travel-tax and terminal-fee exemption. Treatment of self-sponsored freelance-permit holders is not uniform — confirm your case with DMW or the Migrant Workers Office before booking a flight.

documents.name: Certified proof of Philippine civil status (PSA birth / marriage certificate, apostilled and UAE-Embassy attested)
documents.description: PSA-issued birth certificate, and marriage certificate if married, apostilled by DFA and attested by the UAE Embassy in Manila. Not needed for the freelance permit itself but required later for family sponsorship, school enrolment and some bank/insurance formalities — process it while still in the Philippines.
documents.source: Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) / UAE Embassy in Manila

documents.name: UAE entry permit (residence entry visa) sponsored by the free zone
documents.description: Electronic entry permit issued by ICP or GDRFA through the freelance-licence issuing authority; Filipino nationals are not eligible for visa-on-arrival unless holding a valid US/UK/EU/Australian/Canadian visa or residence permit, so the entry permit must be issued before travel and activated on arrival.
documents.source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

documents.name: Establishment card / immigration file card of the freelance licence
documents.description: Immigration establishment card issued in the freelancer's own licence name (e.g. AED 2,000 under GoFreelance), which is the mechanism that allows the licence to sponsor the holder's residence visa and, later, dependants.

documents.name: UAE medical fitness certificate
documents.description: Screening at a government-approved centre (Dubai Health/Smart Salem, Emirates Health Services elsewhere) for HIV and tuberculosis — plus syphilis/Hepatitis B for certain occupations. Must be taken after the entry permit is issued and before visa stamping and Emirates ID issuance; applicants must be 18+.

documents.name: Valid UAE health insurance policy
documents.description: Health cover meeting the minimum benefit standards of the emirate of residence (DHA for Dubai, DOH for Abu Dhabi). Self-sponsored freelancers must buy their own policy; the residence file is not completed without it.

documents.name: Emirates ID application with biometric enrolment
documents.description: Application submitted to ICP (or via an Amer/typing centre) followed by in-person fingerprint and facial capture at an ICP or authorised enrolment centre. Residency becomes fully active once the Emirates ID is issued.
documents.source: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)

documents.name: Issued residence visa (e-visa / residence permit linked to the freelance licence)
documents.description: The 1- or 2-year self-sponsored residence permit issued after the medical certificate and Emirates ID biometrics are cleared; issued electronically by ICP or GDRFA Dubai rather than as a passport sticker in most cases.
documents.source: General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs – Dubai (GDRFA)

documents.name: MOFAIC (UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs) attestation of Philippine documents
documents.description: Final in-country legalisation stamp on the degree, PSA and other Philippine certificates already attested in Manila. Required before UAE bodies (licensing authorities, employers, schools, courts) will accept them; documents lacking the Manila embassy step are commonly rejected at this stage.

documents.name: Registered UAE mobile number in the applicant's own name
documents.description: A local SIM registered against the passport/Emirates ID; required by freelance-permit issuers and used for all ICP, medical-test and banking OTP verifications.

documents.name: Registered tenancy contract (Ejari or emirate equivalent)
documents.description: Attested lease registration in the freelancer's name, used as proof of address for utilities, family sponsorship and bank compliance updates. Registered via Ejari in Dubai; equivalent tenancy registration systems apply in other emirates.

documents.name: UAE personal bank account file (freelance licence + Emirates ID + address proof)
documents.description: A freelance licence holder may open a personal account and receive client payments, but cannot hire staff without converting to an LLC. Banks apply their own KYC list on top of the licence, Emirates ID and tenancy proof.

documents.name: Annual freelance licence and residence visa renewal file
documents.description: The freelance permit is renewed yearly (fees roughly equal to setup cost) and the residence visa every 1–2 years, each renewal requiring a fresh TB screening, current health insurance and valid passport.

documents.name: OWWA membership and Philippine Consulate/MWO registration
documents.description: Overseas Workers Welfare Administration membership and registration with the Migrant Workers Office (Philippine Consulate General Dubai for Dubai and the Northern Emirates, Philippine Embassy Abu Dhabi otherwise) — needed for welfare benefits, exit-clearance processing and passport/civil-registry services while resident. Optional for permit issuance, strongly advisable for stability.

documents.name: UAE Federal Tax Authority registration (corporate tax / VAT, if thresholds met)
documents.description: Freelance licence income above the corporate-tax threshold, or taxable turnover above the VAT registration threshold, triggers registration and filing obligations with the FTA. Thresholds and small-business relief change — verify your position directly with the Federal Tax Authority.

documents.name: Philippine passport (valid, machine-readable)
documents.description: DFA-issued Philippine passport for the principal applicant and each accompanying family member; passport bio-data page is uploaded to the e-APR and the passport number must match the Express Entry profile. Must remain valid through landing, since the COPR/PR visa is tied to the passport.

documents.name: PSA birth certificate (Security Paper / SECPA)
documents.description: Philippine Statistics Authority-issued birth certificate on security paper for the applicant and each dependent child, showing full name, date of birth and parents' names. If the PSA record is unreadable or 'negative', a Certificate of No Record plus a Local Civil Registry copy is normally requested.

documents.name: PSA marriage certificate, CENOMAR, or annulment/divorce decree
documents.description: PSA-issued civil status record: marriage certificate for a spouse being included, or CENOMAR (Certificate of No Marriage Record) if single, or a court-issued annulment/nullity decision with PSA annotation for prior marriages. <cite index="2-3">Marriage certificates, divorce decrees, death certificates or other civil status documents are required where applicable.</cite>

documents.name: NBI Multi-purpose Clearance Certificate (police certificate)
documents.description: The Philippine police certificate IRCC accepts is the <cite index="16-2">National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) Multi-purpose Clearance Certificate</cite>. <cite index="16-6">It must bear a thumbprint and include a dry seal</cite>, and <cite index="16-7">no translation is required because it is issued in English</cite>. It must be issued for travel/immigration abroad, not local employment. <cite index="16-8">Certificates must be picked up in person unless the requestor lives outside the Philippines, in which case they are mailed.</cite> Required for the applicant and every family member aged 18 or older.

documents.name: NBI Form No. 5 fingerprint card consularized by a Philippine Consulate
documents.description: Only needed if you are outside the Philippines when applying: <cite index="13-2,13-3,13-4,13-5">the Philippine Consulate General consularizes NBI Form No. 5 (Fingerprint Card form), which is required to obtain the NBI Clearance from the Philippines; applicants then send the completed form to the NBI.</cite> Verify the current procedure with the consulate serving your area, as steps differ per post.

documents.name: Police certificate from each other country of residence
documents.description: Separate from the NBI clearance: <cite index="11-13">if you have lived in another country for six consecutive months or more since the age of 18, you must also obtain a police certificate from that country</cite> — highly relevant for Filipinos with prior work in UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Singapore, Hong Kong or Taiwan.

documents.name: Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) report
documents.description: Assessment of your Philippine diploma/transcript by an IRCC-designated organization. <cite index="8-14">You need to get your foreign educational credential assessed by one of IRCC's approved third parties.</cite> <cite index="12-2">WES, ICAS and IQAS all accept Philippine credentials.</cite> The ECA report is a distinct document from the underlying diploma and Transcript of Records, which some assessors require to be sent directly by your school.

documents.name: Language test results (IELTS General Training, CELPIP, PTE Core or TEF/TCF)
documents.description: Original test report from an IRCC-designated provider taken within the last two years. <cite index="8-17">For all three Express Entry programs you must take English and/or French test(s) and score enough points to be eligible.</cite> Only the General/immigration versions are accepted — academic versions are not.

documents.name: Employer reference/experience letters for each declared job
documents.description: Letters on company letterhead from each Philippine or overseas employer stating job title, dates of employment, hours worked per week, annual salary plus benefits, and detailed duties matching your NOC code. <cite index="7-11,7-12">A reference letter that omits hours, salary or duties is the most common avoidable cause of refusal.</cite> For OFW experience, keep the POEA/DMW-verified contract as supporting evidence.

documents.name: Proof of settlement funds (official bank letter/certification)
documents.description: Bank-issued letter on letterhead with account numbers, opening dates, current and six-month average balances, and outstanding debts, for FSWP/FSTP applicants. <cite index="30-10,30-11,30-12">Canadian Experience Class applicants do not need to show settlement funds</cite>, and <cite index="30-13">applicants with a valid job offer are also exempt.</cite> Amounts are <cite index="26-1">updated annually based on 50% of the low-income cut-off (LICO)</cite> — sources disagree on the exact 2026 figures, so confirm the current table on the IRCC proof-of-funds page for your family size. Philippine peso balances are converted to CAD.

documents.name: Digital photo for the Express Entry application
documents.description: One recent digital photograph per applicant meeting IRCC's immigration photo specifications, uploaded to the e-APR. This is distinct from your biometrics photo captured at a collection point and from the separate PR card photo requested later in the PR portal.

documents.name: Biometrics enrolment (fingerprints and photo) at a VAC
documents.description: <cite index="7-7">After you submit, you are typically asked to give biometrics</cite> at a Visa Application Centre — in the Philippines this is done at VFS Global offices in Manila or Cebu after receiving the Biometrics Instruction Letter. <cite index="16-1">Giving fingerprints for a police certificate is not the same as giving your biometrics for an application.</cite> Bring the instruction letter and your passport.

documents.name: Immigration Medical Examination (IME) by an IRCC panel physician
documents.description: Completed at an IRCC-designated panel physician clinic in the Philippines. <cite index="8-6,8-7">You no longer need an upfront medical exam before submitting an Express Entry application — you upload a blank document in that field and wait for IRCC's instructions on when to get the exam.</cite> Keep the eMedical/IME reference number for your file.

documents.name: PRC professional licence and board certification (regulated occupations)
documents.description: Applies to Filipino nurses, engineers, teachers, accountants and other regulated professionals. <cite index="12-8">PRC licence documents are often required separately for nursing/healthcare applicants.</cite> Also useful later for provincial credential recognition; verify the exact evidence with the relevant Canadian regulator.

documents.name: CFO Guidance and Counselling Certificate and emigrant registration sticker
documents.description: Philippine exit requirement, not a Canadian one. <cite index="20-3">The CFO has confirmed that Filipinos departing with immigrant or long-term permanent residence visas must secure the Guidance and Counselling Program prior to departure.</cite> <cite index="24-2">The CFO emigrant registration sticker must be presented to Philippine Bureau of Immigration officers before departure.</cite> Register via the CFO's online system (OF-CORS); confirm current fees and appointment rules directly with CFO.

documents.name: Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR / eCOPR)
documents.description: Issued after approval and presented to a CBSA officer at your port of entry to complete landing. It is your proof of status until the PR card arrives — <cite index="42-5">while you wait for your PR card you can use your signed confirmation of permanent residence to apply for a social insurance number and access government programs.</cite> Keep the original plus digital copies permanently.

documents.name: Goods to Follow and Goods Accompanying lists (BSF186 / BSF186A)
documents.description: Two typed inventories of personal effects — one for items you carry in and one for items shipped later — declared to CBSA at first landing so household goods enter duty- and tax-free as settler's effects. Include values, serial numbers and (for balikbayan boxes) the shipping manifest. Lists cannot be added after you land.

documents.name: Canadian mailing address notification to IRCC
documents.description: Not a certificate but a mandatory filing: <cite index="42-3,42-4">if you did not provide a Canadian mailing address when you became a permanent resident, use IRCC's online address notification tool within 180 days to avoid cancellation of your PR card — otherwise you must apply for another one and pay new processing fees.</cite> Keep the confirmation and a lease or utility bill as proof of address.

documents.name: Social Insurance Number (SIN)
documents.description: Nine-digit number from Service Canada needed to work, file taxes and receive benefits. Apply with your COPR/eCOPR and passport; <cite index="38-14">original documents only are accepted — photocopies are not.</cite> A PR SIN begins with 4, 5 or 6 rather than the 9 used for temporary residents.

documents.name: Provincial or territorial health insurance card
documents.description: Apply in the province where you settle (e.g. OHIP in Ontario, MSP in British Columbia, AHCIP in Alberta) using your COPR, passport and proof of provincial address. Waiting periods and required proofs differ by province — <cite index="40-15">Alberta, for example, can cover arrivals from the date residency is established if you apply within three months</cite> — so verify with your provincial ministry. Consider private interim coverage for any gap.

documents.name: Permanent Resident (PR) card
documents.description: Your official status and travel document, issued from the photo collected in the PR portal — <cite index="42-7,42-8,42-9">IRCC asks for a photo to start making your first PR card, you don't apply for it, and it is mailed to the Canadian address you provided.</cite> <cite index="37-1">If you travel outside Canada without a valid PR card, you must apply for a permanent resident travel document before returning by commercial carrier.</cite>

documents.name: Provincial driver's licence with Philippine LTO driving record
documents.description: To convert or reduce graduated-licensing steps, most provinces ask for your valid LTO licence plus an official LTO/Philippine driving abstract or certification of driving history; some accept it only if authenticated. Requirements differ by province and the Philippines has no full reciprocity in most provinces — verify with the provincial licensing authority.

documents.name: Residency-day records for PR status maintenance and citizenship
documents.description: Keep boarding passes, passport stamps, lease agreements and CRA Notices of Assessment as evidence of physical presence: <cite index="37-9">to keep PR status you must have been in Canada at least 730 days during the last five years.</cite> The same records support a later citizenship application, which uses a separate 1,095-day threshold.

documents.name: Dual citizenship / Philippine passport renewal record
documents.description: Canada permits dual citizenship, and the Philippines allows natural-born Filipinos who later naturalize to retain or reacquire citizenship under RA 9225 through a Philippine Consulate. Retain your PSA birth certificate and Philippine passport for any future reacquisition or Report of Marriage/Birth filings; confirm current procedures with the consulate serving your province.
documents.source: Philippine Department of Foreign Affairs / Philippine Consulate General (Canada)

documents.name: German passport or national identity card (Personalausweis)
documents.description: Sole entry document needed. IMPORTANT: as a German (EU) national you are outside the scope of the D8 digital nomad visa, which Portugal grants only to non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals; you enter and stay under EU free movement (Lei n.º 37/2006) with just a valid ID or passport for the first 3 months, and no consular visa application exists for your nationality. Card/passport must be valid for the whole stay.

documents.name: NIF (Número de Identificação Fiscal) attribution request
documents.description: Portuguese 9-digit tax number issued by Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira. Can be requested free of charge in advance at a Portuguese consulate in Germany, or in person after arrival at any Serviço de Finanças / Loja do Cidadão with your ID; needed for a lease, utilities and bank account. As an EU citizen you do not need a fiscal representative once registered as resident.

documents.name: Remote employment contract or freelance/client service agreements
documents.description: Written proof of your remote professional activity (employer contract, or client contracts/invoices if self-employed). Not filed with any consulate for Germans, but used to substantiate the sworn declaration of subordinate or independent professional activity at the Câmara Municipal, and for Finanças/Segurança Social registration.

documents.name: A1 certificate (A1-Bescheinigung) or Portuguese social security liability confirmation
documents.source: Deutsche Verbindungsstelle Krankenversicherung – Ausland (DVKA) / Deutsche Rentenversicherung
documents.description: If you continue working for a German employer while living in Portugal, obtain the EU A1 form determining which country's social security applies; if instead you become self-employed/insured in Portugal, no A1 is issued and you register with Segurança Social locally. Verify your specific case with DVKA/Deutsche Rentenversicherung before departure.

documents.name: European Health Insurance Card (EHIC / EU-Krankenversicherungskarte) or private health insurance policy
documents.description: Health cover proof for the transition period. EHIC covers only temporary/necessary care, not settled residence; German statutory cover normally ends when residence moves, so plan Portuguese SNS enrolment or private cover. Portuguese law may require proof of health insurance for non-employed EU registrants where Germany requires the same of Portuguese citizens — verify with the municipality.

documents.name: Abmeldung confirmation (Abmeldebescheinigung) from German municipal registry
documents.description: Deregistration certificate from your German Einwohnermeldeamt/Bürgeramt when you give up your German residence. Relevant for German tax residence, broadcasting fee and health insurance termination; keep the confirmation as evidence of the move date.

documents.name: Recent bank statements evidencing sufficient resources
documents.description: Statements (typically last 3 months) showing income/savings enough to support yourself without recourse to Portuguese social assistance. Required chiefly if you register as economically self-sufficient rather than as employed/self-employed in Portugal; there is no fixed legal threshold — municipalities in practice look for income around or above the national minimum wage. Note: the D8 income thresholds (4x minimum wage) do NOT apply to German citizens.

documents.name: Portuguese rental contract, property deed or landlord accommodation declaration
documents.description: Document proving your address in the municipality where you will register. Municipalities such as Porto may additionally ask for the electronic rent receipt (Recibo de Renda Eletrónico) or Modelo II lease communication from Autoridade Tributária alongside the lease.

documents.name: Atestado de residência from the Junta de Freguesia
documents.description: Parish-issued residence attestation, accepted as an alternative address proof where you have no lease in your own name (e.g. shared housing, staying with a partner). Distinct from the lease itself; only needed if your municipality requests it — requirements vary by câmara.

documents.name: Declaração sob compromisso de honra (sworn declaration of activity or self-sufficiency)
documents.description: Standard form, provided free at the Câmara Municipal counter and signed in person, declaring either that you carry out subordinate or independent professional activity in Portugal, or that you have sufficient resources (and health insurance where applicable) for yourself and family under Article 7 of Lei n.º 37/2006.

documents.name: CRUE – Certificado de Registo de Cidadão da União Europeia
documents.description: Your actual residence document as a German citizen — this replaces the D8 residence permit route entirely. Requested in person (physical presence mandatory, no proxy) at the Câmara Municipal or Loja do Cidadão of your area of residence within 30 days after completing 3 months in Portugal, i.e. roughly between day 90 and day 120. Fee approx. €15 for adults; validity 5 years. Do not book an AIMA appointment for this.

documents.name: NISS (Número de Identificação de Segurança Social) registration
documents.source: Instituto da Segurança Social (Segurança Social Direta)
documents.description: Social security number obtained from Instituto da Segurança Social, normally after the CRUE. Needed if you work, invoice or pay contributions in Portugal; not needed if an A1 certificate keeps you insured in Germany — confirm your situation with Segurança Social.

documents.name: Declaração de início de atividade with Autoridade Tributária
documents.description: Self-employment/freelancer opening declaration filed at Finanças or on Portal das Finanças, required only if you invoice clients as an independent worker from Portugal. Not needed if you remain a salaried employee of a foreign company.

documents.name: Número de Utente do SNS (national health service user number)
documents.source: Serviço Nacional de Saúde (SNS) / Ministério da Saúde
documents.description: Registration at your local Centro de Saúde to access public healthcare, normally requiring CRUE, NIF and address proof. Some health centres also ask for the NISS — verify locally as practice varies by unit.

documents.name: Change of fiscal address / tax residency registration with Autoridade Tributária
documents.description: Update of your NIF record from non-resident to resident at your Portuguese address, which triggers Portuguese tax residency and annual IRS filing obligations. Coordinate with the Germany–Portugal double taxation treaty to avoid dual residence.

documents.name: IFICI application (tax incentive for scientific research and innovation, successor to NHR)
documents.source: Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira (Portal das Finanças)
documents.description: Optional application for the Portuguese preferential tax regime, submitted to Autoridade Tributária by 15 January of the year after you become tax resident; the deadline is generally not recoverable if missed. Eligibility is activity-based — confirm with AT or a licensed Portuguese accountant.

documents.name: German EU driving licence registration with IMT
documents.source: Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes (IMT)
documents.description: A German EU licence stays valid in Portugal, but residents are expected to register it (or exchange it) with Instituto da Mobilidade e dos Transportes after establishing residence. Deadlines and whether registration is mandatory in your case should be verified directly with IMT.

documents.name: Certificado de Residência Permanente para Nacionais UE
documents.description: Permanent residence certificate for EU nationals, applied for through AIMA after 5 years of continuous legal residence in Portugal; renewal of an expired CRUE is likewise handled by AIMA rather than the municipality.
